# An effect handler with no statements is a function that returns, and still
# declared, since `@update {}` decides which handler a write reaches
# (effect_changes_runs.txt). `@mount(k) {}` became a function with an empty
# body, which the Go emitter writes as a signature and
# so as no method at all, and the call the effect makes to it did not build on
# bubbletea, fyne or gtk4 ("m.__effect0_mount undefined"), in the component's
# body and in an instance built per copy alike.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import seq "sngl:seq"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component asker(n int) ui.node {
    effect(on=n, @mount(k) {})
}

component page ui.node {
    var count = 2

    for var i = seq.count(count) {
        asker(n=i)
    }
    ui.button #more(text="More", @click { count += 1 })
}

func testAnEmptyMountBuilds(t test.Test, c page) {
    c.more.click()
    t.assert(c.count == 3)
}

ui.window {
    page()
}
